summary: Discovery call for a pilot to evaluate Redwood API for Neptulex's customer-facing summarization product. Key concerns: latency SLOs, data residency, cost vs latency tradeoffs, and private deployment requirements for regulated clients. Team agreed to a sandbox quickstart, security packet, and a benchmark run focusing on streaming + KV cache performance.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) tradeoffs
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
performance: latency SLOs, KV cache, batching
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Neptulex CTO), Meera Patel (ML Engineer), Dylan Ho (Platform)
Links shared: sandbox quickstart (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart), security pack (note: sent after call), pilot pricing spreadsheet (drive link note)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for doing this, can you hear me ok?
00:06 Carlos: yeah loud and clear, thanks for setting this up, excited to understand the path to ship this pilot
00:12 Samira: hi all, quick intro — i'm samira, i'll be running the benchmark work with you and helping map constraints to the right hosting option
00:20 Carlos: great, quick context — Neptulex is building a summarization service for enterprise docs, some customers require strict data residency and audit trails, others are fine with hosted. we want to understand if we can go hosted first and move to dedicated or private for specific customers.
00:35 Jordan: perfect — the typical path we see is self-serve API to time-to-first-token, then a small dedicated capacity pilot or VPC staging if you need isolation. do you have an initial traffic estimate or SLO for latency?
00:48 Meera: we're aiming for 95 pctl < 300ms token latency for short interactions, and end-to-end summary generation under 1.2s for average doc snippets. throughput is modest to start, ~50 req/s peak, but bursts during morning syncs.
01:05 Dylan: also important — our infra uses GCP in eu-west1, and data residency will matter for eu customers. Can Redwood route to regionally-hosted endpoints?
01:16 Samira: yes, we have regional model endpoints and routing policies. hosted API supports region routing and fallbacks; dedicated and private give you control over the cluster region. note: for private on-prem or VPC we do an installer or image that runs in your network.
01:32 Carlos: cool. two constraints: SOC2 is required and we need KMS integration for encryption at rest, plus SSO for our console ops.
01:41 Jordan: we can share SOC2 and ISO docs, SAML/SSO is supported, and we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; hosted has customer key options via KMS as well — we'll send the full security pack after.
01:53 Meera: about cost, we want to understand tradeoffs — do you have guidance on batching and token-cost optimization? our prompts are often repetitive prefixes, so prefix caching could help right?
02:06 Samira: yep, automatic prefix/KV caching is in our runtime, that reduces per-token compute. we also recommend quantized model variants for dedicated/private if cost is a concern. for hosted, we expose profiles and cost-per-token estimates in the console.
02:20 Carlos: does the quickstart give us streaming responses? we rely on streaming to show partial summaries fast to users.
02:27 Jordan: Streaming and function-calling are supported on the API; time-to-first-token for a simple call usually under a couple hundred ms in hosted eu region in our tests but we'll need to benchmark with your prompt set and sequence length.
03:01 Dylan: can you clarify what "time-to-first-token" means in practice? some vendors quote model response times ignoring cold-starts and routing overheads.
03:10 Samira: good point — our published numbers are median steady-state token latency. for end-to-end ttf token we include network and routing; cold starts can add extra ~100-300ms depending on model variant and if the model is warmed. for your pilot we can keep a warm pool or use dedicated to reduce cold starts.
03:40 Carlos: for compliance customers we may need private deployment (VPC or on-prem). how long does it take to stand up private?
03:48 Samira: private VPC deployment typically 2-4 weeks for initial onboarding if infra is ready; on-prem can take longer depending on firewall and air-gap. dedicated (reserved capacity) can be quicker if it's just a region and we allocate GPUs, often within a week for standard configs.
04:05 Meera: what's included in the sandbox quickstart? i want to get a dev experience where i can call endpoints from our CI and iterate prompts.
04:14 Jordan: sandbox includes API keys with free credits, a quickstart repo, example SDK usage for node/python, and a small sample dataset to try embeddings and generation. time-to-first-token for a basic test should be under 30 minutes from signup once you configure your key.
04:30 Carlos: awesome — is there any rate limiting on the sandbox?
04:33 Jordan: limited quotas for fair usage; we'll set your voucher so you can run benchmark-scale tests as part of the pilot.
04:39 Dylan: curious about model variants — do you allow pinning a specific model version and automatic fallback to a smaller variant if capacity hits?
04:45 Samira: yes, rollouts allow pinning; routing policies can fallback to compatible variants. you can do canary and A/B traffic splits in the console.
05:00 Meera: for the benchmark, we need streaming with 8k token context and KV cache behavior — any specific artifacts you need from us?
05:10 Samira: please share representative prompts, average sequence lengths, and a desired SLO table (p95/p99). we'll run continuous-batching tests and measure per-token latency, throughput, and memory use.
05:24 Carlos: expected timeline — we want a pilot in the next 4 weeks. ideally start with hosted quickstart and then evaluate dedicated for production tenants.
05:33 Jordan: makes sense. recommended path: immediate sandbox + quickstart to validate quality and integration, then a 2-week dedicated pilot to test sustained throughput and dedication. if some customers require private, we scope VPC pilot in parallel.
05:51 Dylan: if we go dedicated, how does autoscaling and burst capacity work? we have diurnal loads and burst events.
05:58 Samira: dedicated pools support autoscaling policies and burst credits; you can configure min/max pool size and a burst window. we also expose token-level cost breakdown and latency heatmaps in the console so you can tune batching and scaling.
06:18 Carlos: security question — does hosted retain customer data for model fine-tuning or logs? we need audit logs for requests and retention controls.
06:27 Jordan: hosted does not use your data to train public models. we provide request audit logs, retention policies, and per-request PII redaction rules for enterprise plans. private gives full control over logs and retention in your environment.
06:41 Meera: integrations — we need SAML SSO and RBAC; does Redwood have granular roles for developer vs ops?
06:48 Samira: yes, RBAC is supported with role templates and SAML SSO. we can map your IdP groups to roles.
07:01 Carlos: any gotchas around KV cache invalidation if we have frequently updated templates?
07:07 Samira: cache is prefix-based; if prompt prefix changes frequently you lose cache benefits. we recommend stable system prompts and moving mutable context to embeddings/metadata lookups. we'll demo cache behavior in the benchmark.
07:26 Meera: about pricing — can you ballpark cost for 50 req/s sustained on a 8k context model?
07:33 Jordan: ballpark depends on model family; hosted standard variants cost X units per 1k tokens — i'll avoid raw numbers on this call but we'll send the pilot pricing sheet with scenarios for hosted/dedicated/private. we'll also include guidance on quantized instances to reduce unit cost.
07:52 Dylan: are there limits for KV cache size per model?
07:56 Samira: limits are configurable; for hosted we expose reasonable defaults, for dedicated/private you can configure cache sizes and node memory to match.
08:10 Carlos: any reference customers in regulated verticals? we want examples we can talk to.
08:16 Jordan: yes — we have a couple of healthcare and finance customers; i'll check NDA constraints and connect you with a reference.
08:24 Meera: about SDKs — do you have a streaming websocket SDK or only HTTP streaming?
08:29 Samira: we have HTTP streaming and websocket SDKs in alpha for some languages; Node and Python have mature clients with streaming support.
08:38 Carlos: ok next steps — i'd like that sandbox + pricing + security pack. we also want to run the benchmark before the next exec review.
08:47 Jordan: noted. we'll provision the sandbox today and send the security pack + pricing. what's a good date for the benchmark window?
08:55 Carlos: propose 2026-03-31 or 2026-04-01, midday CET. Dylan will coordinate infra details.
09:03 Dylan: sounds good, i'll share our prompt set and a small harness to drive requests.
09:08 Samira: great, i'll prepare a benchmark plan and what metrics we'll capture (p95/p99 token latency, throughput, memory, cold-starts, streaming tail latency).
09:18 Meera: one last note — we expect some customers to demand EU-only hosting, can Redwood guarantee data residency for hosted EU region?
09:27 Jordan: we can route to EU regions and provide data residency controls; for legal guarantees we often recommend dedicated or private for strict SLA/residency contracts. we'll include language in the security pack.
09:38 Carlos: perfect, thanks. anything else?
09:41 Jordan: just to recap: we'll send sandbox creds + 1k credits, security pack, pilot pricing; Samira will send benchmark plan; Neptulex to share prompts and SLOs; schedule benchmark for 2026-03-31.
09:56 Carlos: great, talk soon — thanks everyone.
10:01 End meeting.

Notes on transcription: some terms like "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash" at times; "quantized" heard as "quan-tized"; occasional speaker label jitter.
